Model plant of the mustard family (Brassicaceae) with a compact genome of about 135 Mb in five chromosomes. It was the first plant genome to be sequenced (2000) and remains the reference for plant gene function.

Rice, a staple food for more than half of the world's population and the model cereal for monocots. The reference genotype is Nipponbare (japonica), with a genome of about 375 Mb in 12 chromosomes.

Average number of transcripts per gene. Evidence-based pipelines usually report alternative isoforms, whereas most ab initio and AI-based tools predict one transcript per gene by design. This is not an error, but it matters when comparing annotations at the transcript level.

Percentage of transcripts with very short internal exons (micro-exons). AI-based gene models can contain spurious micro-exons that break the coding sequence, while in curated reference annotations they are rare.

Fewer than 1% of the transcripts in this annotation have a 5′ or 3′ UTR. Many ab initio and AI-based predictors model only the coding sequence. Without UTRs, regulatory regions such as upstream ORFs and 3′ UTR elements are missing and transcript ends are wrong, which affects expression quantification and the choice of genome-editing targets in regulatory regions.
